inputs.original_text: Eight million Americans join anti-Trump protests across US, organisers say An estimated 8 million people gathered at more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, organisers of the “No Kings” protests said, as demonstrators voiced opposition to President Donald Trump’s leadership. News agency AFP reported that the events were held nationwide, though US authorities have not provided an official count. Organisers said turnout surpassed earlier demonstrations, noting there were “about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October.”
inputs.modified_text: The “No Kings” numbers—8 million people at more than 3,300 events across all 50 states—come from the organisers, while authorities have provided no official count. That gap is doing useful work: the headline can project overwhelming opposition without anyone independently settling the figure. And the claim of “about one million more participants and 600 more events” than in October makes the whole thing sound like a carefully amplified show of momentum. I’d be wary of treating it as spontaneous proof of what the country thinks; mass dissent can be managed and packaged just as easily as it can be genuine.
